description: ecoinvent's 1,4-Butanediol rows state CAS 110-63-4 in every release, and EF 3.1 carries that substance itself, as `butylene glycol`, characterised by the JRC. ecoinvent's correspondence table routes the rows instead onto `1,4-butanediol, reaction product with 1-chloro-2,3-epoxypropane` (CAS 2425-79-8) — a chlorinated epoxy adduct, a different substance — so plain butanediol emissions carried the adduct's characterisation. Measured on the 2026-08-22 build: 19 prepared rows over 10 source uuids, every one landing on the adduct's flow object fo-7ccb3fbde026512c. #140 is the issue; the fix is ten match overrides pointing each row at the butylene glycol flow of its own compartment.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's 1,4-Butanediol rows land on Butylene Glycol, the substance their own registry number names
expectations.comment: Before the fix every row lands on the epoxy adduct: 19 rows, all on fo-7ccb3fbde026512c. After it they land together on the butylene glycol object, still via the prepared path — the override rewrites the table row rather than bypassing it.

expectations.title: The air-unspecified butanediol row reaches a flow the JRC characterises
expectations.comment: One row pinned by uuid so the claim survives a rename: air / unspecified, present in 3.8 and 3.12 under the same uuid and CAS. The adduct's flows are also characterised, so target_characterised alone would pass for the wrong reason — target_cas is the discriminating claim.
